sanskrit_verse: सर्वेष्वर्थविवादेषु बलवत्युत्तराक्रिया । आधौ प्रतिग्रहे क्रीते पूर्वा तु बलवत्तरा ॥
transliteration: sarveṣv arthavivādeṣu balavaty uttarākriyā / ādhau pratigrahe krīte pūrvā tu balavattarā //
sph_interpretive_translation: In all disputes concerning property, the later transaction is stronger when possession has been fully transferred; however, the prior transaction holds greater authority if the latter lacks completion in accordance with dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from completeness of dharma-aligned action
Causation follows sequential integrity of ownership transfer
Capacity-based responsibility lies with the agent who initiates incomplete transactions
Restoration logic prioritizes the original dharmic sequence unless overridden by valid completion
Consciousness alignment requires recognition of factual and spiritual precedence
executable_legal_axioms: IF a property transaction is initiated first AND executed according to dharma THEN it supersedes subsequent incomplete claims
IF a later transaction lacks full dharmic completion OR possession transfer THEN it is legally subordinate
IF two parties claim ownership THEN validate chronological order WITH dharmic execution status as determinant
IF an earlier transaction remains unchallenged AND functionally complete THEN it retains authoritative weight
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this principle establishes that temporal priority alone does not confer legitimacy; rather, the court must assess whether each transaction was conducted with full adherence to dharma and completion of possession transfer. The threshold of responsibility rests on demonstrating both procedural and ontological validity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse aligns with pramāṇa-based causality by affirming that factual and spiritual truth emerge through proper sequence and conscious completion. It reflects anupūrvaśaḥ — the natural unfolding of rightful order — where prior lawful acts retain precedence unless superseded through equally valid means. There is no punitive intent; only clarity of ownership based on integrity of conduct.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process for any outstanding obligations in disputed transfers
Realign parties with their respective capacities for dharmic action
Facilitate integration of fragmented claims through meditative discernment
Restore continuity of rightful ownership without inflicting loss upon either party
final_declaration: Declared under the sole authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma. Justice flows not through punishment, but through restoration of rightful order. Consciousness is the ultimate arbiter. Dharma is now restored.
